title: xiom verify
concept: The xiom verify command runs Z3 on your contracts, attempting to mathematically prove they hold for all possible inputs.
why: Runtime checks are great for debugging, but static verification proves correctness for ALL inputs — the gold standard of software reliability.
theory:
## Running xiom verify

```sh
# Verify a single file
xiom verify src/math.xi

# Verify all files in a directory
xiom verify src/**/*.xi

# Verify with specific options
xiom verify --timeout 30 --solver z3 src/math.xi
```

### Reading the Output

```
=== Verification Results ===

Function: divide
  requires: b != 0
    Status: ASSUMED (precondition — caller's responsibility)
  ensures: result * b == a
    Status: ✓ PROVED (holds for all inputs satisfying requires)

Function: factorial
  requires: n >= 0
    Status: ASSUMED
  ensures: result > 0
    Status: ✗ UNKNOWN (recursive function — Z3 couldn't prove)
    Hint: Add loop invariant or use inductive proof

  Summary: 3 proved, 0 failed, 1 unknown, 2 assumed
```

### Understanding Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| PROVED | Contract proven for all inputs |
| FAILED | Counterexample found — contract can be violated |
| UNKNOWN | Z3 couldn't determine — may need more constraints |
| ASSUMED | Precondition assumed true, not verified |
| TIMEOUT | Verification took too long |

### Proving ensures

For ensures to be PROVED, Z3 must show that for ALL inputs satisfying the requires, the ensures holds after the function body executes.

### CI Integration
```yaml
# GitHub Actions
- name: Verify contracts
  run: xiom verify src/**/*.xi
```
syntax_ref:
# Run verification:
xiom verify file.xi

# With timeout (seconds):
xiom verify --timeout 60 file.xi

# Verbose output:
xiom verify --verbose file.xi
tips: Start with simple functions — Z3 handles arithmetic and booleans best
Look for UNKNOWN results — they indicate functions where Z3 needs more help (loop invariants, etc.)
Run xiom verify as part of your CI pipeline — catch contract regressions automatically
PROVED ensures is the highest confidence you can have in a function's correctness
common_mistakes: Expecting Z3 to prove everything — some properties require interactive theorem provers
Ignoring UNKNOWN results — they may hide real bugs
Not writing complete enough contracts — Z3 can only prove what you specify
